chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the owned slave is blinded, he has been emancipated.

key_terms.عَمِيَ: to be blinded / to lose sight

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave who becomes blind?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing that blindness serves as an automatic cause for emancipation (itq) without requiring a master's declaration. This principle reflects the Shia juristic view that physical impairments like blindness or leprosy constitute inherent value (qimah) that, when lost, entitle the slave to freedom, highlighting the merciful dimension of manumission in Islamic law.
